name: prefers-contrast
plain: OS setting for higher or lower color contrast.
meaning: Signals low vision or light sensitivity. Values no-preference, more, less, custom. Rare, so each non-default value is highly distinguishing.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell if you asked your device for more or less contrast
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Check whether you chose more, less or normal contrast
Add the answer to a browser fingerprint
cannot: Tell why you chose it, though it can hint at a vision need

story.what_it_is: Tells a page whether you asked your device for more or less color contrast.

marketing.name: prefers-contrast
marketing.pitch: Documents how a page can notice the person wants higher or lower contrast and adapt its colors.

story.for_you: You never see the check. If you turned on higher contrast, a good site gives you stronger borders and darker text without a menu.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to make pages readable for low vision and bright sunlight. It is also a private fact. The setting may point to a disability, so careful teams do not log it.

use_cases.example: A web app darkens gray text and thickens borders when you ask for more contrast.
A bank dashboard uses stronger chart lines and labels for people who need higher contrast.
A browser puzzle game boosts tile outlines so shapes are clear on a small screen.
A reading app shows pure black on white text and removes pale gray hints.
A learning platform adapts lesson slides for students with low vision.
A team chooses not to record the value because it may reveal a health need.

legit_uses: Respect OS theme and accessibility needs
abuse: Infer disability or setting for fingerprinting
